title: Lamb or Mutton with Rice and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Lamb (or mutton) is the meat of sheep, known for its rich flavor and aroma. Combined with boiled rice and vegetables such as carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens, the dish provides a balanced source of protein, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lamb contains more iron than beef, making it helpful for preventing anemia.
In Mediterranean cuisine, lamb is traditionally seasoned with rosemary, thyme, and mint.
Rice is one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for over 5,000 years.
Broccoli is high in glucosinolates, compounds that support the body’s detoxification processes.
Dark‑green leafy vegetables like spinach and kale provide over 10 million IU of vitamin A per 100 g.

items.title: Rich source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Lamb supplies complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High in iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support immune function and normal nervous system activity.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice delivers steady energy, while fiber from the vegetables helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Lamb and rice provide vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens are rich in vitamin C, carotenoids, and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Some cuts of lamb are rich in saturated fats; choose lean cuts and consume in moderation.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A minority of people may experience allergic reactions to sheep meat.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Lamb contains purines, which can raise uric acid levels in individuals prone to gout.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow bacterial growth such as Salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lamb can be roasted, braised, or pan‑seared and served with boiled rice and lightly sautéed vegetables. Add spices like cumin, coriander, and garlic to enhance flavor. Cook vegetables "al dente" to retain crunch and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw lamb refrigerated at ≤ 4 °C for no more than 2‑3 days, and store cooked dishes in airtight containers for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze the meat in airtight bags and the prepared meal in portioned containers for up to 2 months.
